newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Kabul's main airbase shelled in hit-and-run attack.
newsitem.headline: Kabul's main airbase shelled in hit-and-run attack.

text.p: Forces loyal to the Afghan government ousted two weeks ago shelled Kabul's main airbase at Bagram on Friday in the latest of a series of hit-and-run attacks well behind the front line, witnesses said.
They said at least six shells landed inside the perimeter of the base some 50 km (30 miles) north of Kabul, but it was not immediately known if there was any damage.
The purist Islamic Taleban militia, which drove the forces of former government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood from Kabul on September 27, replied with helicopter gunships.
They fired rockets towards villages and hills to the east of the airbase from where the shelling appeared to be coming, but it was not known if they had hit anything.
Masood's forces used anti-aircraft guns against the gunships, but hit neither, during an exchange of fire that lasted about an hour.

It was the third attack on Taleban positions near Kabul on Friday and there were several behind the militia's front lines two hours' drive north from the capital at Jabal-os-Siraj on Thursday, travellers and witnesses said.
At Saray Khoeja, 15 km (nine miles) south of Bagram, which was evacuated on Thursday amid fears the base would be attacked, local fighters opened fire on Taleban militia, fleeing villagers said.
They said the local fighters attacked after a Masood envoy visited the village to urge them to turn on the Taleban, who have imposed the stern Islamic Sharia law on Kabul.
The Taleban sent two tanks at high speed from Kabul, trailed by a convoy of pick-up trucks carrying heavily armed fighters to help in a counter-attack, witnesses said.
About five km (three miles) away at Qarabagh, there was a heavy exchange of small arms fire and rocket-propelled grenades later on Friday.
Taleban fighters dismissed their opponents as "bandits and robbers", but local people again said the attack was the work of local fighters turning against the militia.

Masood withdrew from Kabul and retreated to his Panjsher Valley stronghold under attack along the way from groups which switched sides to the Taleban, who had contacted them in advance, Afghan watchers said.
They said the Taleban might now be seeing those groups switch sides again, if reports of local people were accurate that Masood envoys were encouraging them to turn against the militia.

On Thursday there were two attacks on Taleban positions between Bagram and Charikar, a town about 30 minutes' drive south of Jabal-os-Siraj at the mouth of the Salang Pass which winds through the Hindu Kush mountains, witnesses said.
Travellers said there was a third on the Taleban-occupied governor's house just outside Charikar and another just south of Jabal-os-Siraj.
They said in each case, local people spoke of Taleban fighters being killed and wounded.
